 15 Best Things To Do This Weekend In Singapore – 6th-8th November 2026 
 Khoo Yong Hao 
 • 
 05 Nov 2026 
 • 
 Events 
 • 
 15 minutes reading time 
 Things to do this weekend in Singapore 
 Kid-friendly activities, live performances, and fun workshops – there’s plenty of fun to be had in the coming weeks. So, open your calendars and bookmark these things to do this weekend in Singapore.
 Table of Contents
 Things to do this weekend in Singapore 1. Zoolympix: Stars of Mandai Festive Challenge 
 2. Warrior 24/7 
 3. Singapore Book Street 2026 
 4. American Tourister The Great Gourmet Getaway 
 5. Singapore Cat Festival 2026 
 6. PokéXciting! 
 7. Snoopy Pop-Up Library 
 8. Me-You Market 
 9. Toy Story | PEACEMINUSONE: The First Fan pop-up 
 10. Deepavali Open House 
 11. Haw Ror Villa 5! – Back From The Dead 
 12. Sunflower Surprise: Garden by the Ocean 
 13. Bollywood Farms 
 14. CATS The Musical 
 15. ONE Ocean: Every Action Ripples 
 1. Zoolympix: Stars of Mandai Festive Challenge 
 7th Nov 2026-3rd Jan 2027 
Image credit: Mandai Wildlife Group 
 This school holidays, Mandai Wildlife Reserve is hosting an epic event called Zoolympix: Stars of Mandai Festive Challenge . Head to the Zoolympix Village at the Mandai Wildlife EAST Lawn to take on 10 challenges inspired by the special abilities of 2 star animals from each of the 5 wildlife parks.
 Each station tests a different skill – from strength and agility, to balance and problem-solving. Through this interactive play, kids not only learn more about these animals, but also find out how they can do their part towards wildlife conservation.
Image credit: Mandai Wildlife Group 
 Collect a stamp for every challenge you clear and get an exclusive Zoolympian medal which you can strike a victory pose with at the Zoolympix Podium. Present those stamps of completion at selected Mandai shops to take home a commemorative Zoolympix plushie for $9 (U.P. $12) .
 The challenges don’t end at the Village either. Seek out Zoolympix Outposts across Singapore Zoo, Bird Paradise, River Wonders, Rainforest Wild Adventure, and Night Safari for bonus challenges inspired by the Stars of Mandai. Along the way, you’ll uncover fascinating animal facts, discover unique abilities, and be encouraged to visit the star animals in their exhibits.
 Between the festive light-ups around the reserve and a Partners Zone packed with games and giveaways, there’s enough to fill a full day out. Plus, locals enjoy access to Zoolympix village plus a $10 retail and F&B voucher when they buy a ticket to selected Mandai attractions.
 While you’re there, make sure to sign the kiddos up for a workshop or 2. There are a whole bunch to choose from, from pizza making and upcycled room scents to a sewing workshop where kids can design and create their very own chou chou plushie from scratch.
 Find out more about Zoolympix at Mandai Wildlife Reserve . 
 Admission: From $15/pax | Local Residents enjoy access to Zoolympix Village
 Venue: 80 Mandai Lake Road, Mandai Wildlife EAST Lawn, Singapore 729826
 Date: 7th November 2026-3rd January 2027
 Time: 10am-7pm, Daily (Last admission at 6.30pm)
 2. Warrior 24/7 
 Now till 15th Nov 
 Image credit: Warrior 24/7 
 Those looking for a meaningful outing this weekend can visit the Warrior 24/7 installation at City Square Mall . Conceived by Parkinson’s disease (PD) advocate and multi-time American Ninja Warrior competitor Jimmy Choi , it’s a showcase of the indomitable fighting spirit that those afflicted with disease display on the daily.
 Image credit: Warrior 24/7 
 It features various stations which invite visitors to step into the shoes of people living with PD. Challenges include fastening buttons with simulated rigidity, picking up fruits with tremor gloves, and testing your balance with wobbling bowls sliding across a food tray.
 Complete all 7 stations, and you’ll be rewarded with a specially designed keychain that serves as a token of camaraderie and respect for the PD community. Also, you can get vouchers for a free bottle of Beutea cold brew tea upon completion of all the stations, redeemable only at the Beutea outlet located within the mall.
 Admission: Free
 Venue: 180 Kitchener Road, City Square Mall, Basement 1, Green Square, Singapore 208539
 Date: 7th-15th November 2026
 Time: 10am-6pm, Daily
 3. Singapore Book Street 2026 
 Now till 8th Nov 
 If you’re on the prowl for your next read, there’s really no better place to look than the ongoing Singapore Book Street 2026 . Set up at VivoCity , it’s the largest book fair on the island that’s purposely dedicated to SingLit , with over 1,200 titles across 4 languages to leaf through.
 It’s also worth noting that a huge chunk of Singapore Book Street 2026’s offerings are eligible for purchase using SG Culture Pass credits , so if you’ve got any left, now’s a great time to use them.
 There’s pretty much every genre you can think of here; when we swung by, we spotted books of all kinds, including fiction, non-fiction, fantasy, poetry, and children’s literature just to name a few. The festival also has other activities such as book signing sessions , interactive storytelling for kids, and even a live typewriter poetry station to get personalised poems.
 Learn more about Singapore Book Street 2026 .
 Admission: Free
 Venue: 180 Kitchener Road, City Square Mall, Basement 1, Green Square, Singapore 208539
 Date: 7th-15th November 2026
 Time: 10am-6pm, Daily
 4. American Tourister The Great Gourmet Getaway 
 9th Oct-30th Nov 
Image credit: American Tourister 
 If you’re gearing up for your next trip, you can warm up with a food trail closer to home. American Tourister has launched The Great Gourmet Getaway , a gastronomical experience taking you through 5 of Singapore’s beloved F&B spots: Birds of Paradise, Chimichanga, Cowpresso, Dumpling Darlings, and Two Men Bagel House. Each stop serves a limited-time, special American Tourister curated menu, and you’ll stamp your way through the trail to unlock sure-win rewards.
 Complete the stamp card and you’ll also be in the running for The Great Giveaway , with prizes worth $200 up for grabs. To qualify, you’ll need to buy a Getaway with American Tourister luggage bundle , visit all 5 food partners, and order the curated menus at each one.
Image credit: American Tourister 
 The bundles start from $199 with the Argyle , which is scratch-resistant and has a multi-pocket interior, plus QUIETO wheels for quiet, smooth gliding. The Tranto , from $299 , is a multi-opening spinner that lets you pack how you want, even in tight spaces, with a quick-access front pocket and Optimov shock-absorbing wheels with StePause technology for better control and stability.
 Find out more about The Great Gourmet Getaway . 
 Locations: Various Birds of Paradise, Chimichanga, Cowpresso, Dumpling Darlings & Two Men Bagel House outlets across Singapore
 Date: 9th October to 30th November 2026
 5. Singapore Cat Festival 2026 
 7th-8th Nov 
 Image credit: Singapore Cat Festival 
 Perhaps the biggest cat-centric event in the entire Little Red Dot, the Singapore Cat Festival is back for its 6th edition, and it’s better than ever. It’ll feature at least 100 curated brands and stalls over 7,000 sqm of space at Singapore EXPO Hall 6 , and the first 1,000 visitors can redeem a free goodie bag that’s filled with treats for your furry friend.
 Image credit: Singapore Cat Festival 
 But shopping for pet supplies to appease your feline overlord ain’t the only thing you can do here. There’s an adoption drive to check out, a CFA Cat Show where you can get up close to all sorts of cats, as well as a silent movie screening that’s perfect for taking a breather. When you’re famished, pop by the F&B zone for bites and beverages.
 Get tickets to Singapore Cat Festival 2026 .
 Admission: From $7/pax
 Venue: 1 Expo Drive, Singapore EXPO, Hall 6, Singapore 486150
 Date: 7th-8th November 2026
 Time: 10am-8pm, Daily
 6. PokéXciting! 
 Now till 3rd Jan 2027 
 If you’re still not in the know, Pokémon is celebrating its 30th anniversary this year – just swing by Changi Airport Terminal 3 and Jewel to see how big of an affair it is. Dubbed PokéXciting! , this 2 month-long celebration spills into 2027 and trust us, you’ll need all the time you can get to experience it in its fullest.
 Peppered around Changi Airport are over 30 Pokémon-themed installations to snap pics with, the centrepiece being a massive Pikachu sculpture posed right in front of Jewel’s Forest Valley. Another impressive one featuring the beloved Eeveelutions resides in the T2 Departure Hall, while T1’s Arrival Garden sports the fan-favourite Charmander and Charizard .
 Over at T3 Departure Hall’s Pokémon Experience Lounge , visitors can try their hand at various Pokémon video game titles such as the recently-released Pokémon Pokopia and Pokémon Champions. For fans of the trading card game, you can duel away at dedicated tables for TCG battles.
 Image credit: Changi Airport Group 
 Happening this weekend only are EDM party sessions at the PokéXciting!” Stage at Terminal 3, as well as a parade that’ll see the appearance of all 27 first partner Pokémon . Of course, you can expect to bring home a huge haul of special 30th anniversary merch too; we’re talking bag charms, figures, travel blankets, insulated tumblers, plushies, and even luggage.
 Learn more about PokéXciting! .
 Admission: Free
 Venue: 60 Airport Boulevard, Changi Airport Terminal 3 & Jewel, Singapore 819643
 Date: Now till 3rd January 2027
 7. Snoopy Pop-Up Library 
 Now till 19th September 2027 
 Whether you’re an OG fan of PEANUTS or looking to introduce the kids to the beloved beagle, a visit to the new Snoopy Pop-Up Library at Plaza Singapura is a must. Set up by the National Library Board (NLB) , it’s a cosy reading nook that encourages children to pick up the good habit of reading, with some help from Snoopy and gang.
 The space is themed after various locations and story beats straight from the PEANUTS comic strips, featuring zones such as Snoopy’s Backyard and Charlie Brown’s Classroom . Within them, photo ops with cut-outs and sculptures of iconic characters await, as well as a huge selection of books that are sure to enthral budding readers and older kids alike.
 Admission: Free
 Venue: 68 Orchard Road, Plaza Singapura, Level 3, #03-86 to 89, Singapore 238839
 Date: Now till 19th September 2027
 Time: 10am-10pm, Daily
 8. Me-You Market 
 7th-8th Nov 
 Image adapted from: Me-You Market 
 Another week, another craft market; this time, Me-You Market ’s flooding *SCAPE and the Suntec City Convention and Exhibition Centre with handmade trinkets, apparel, and yummy F&B options. There’ll be over 180 brands to shop over 2 weekends, so consider your itch for some retail therapy scratched.
 View this post on Instagram 
 What’s more, they’ll be selling some merch of their own too, and the kind folks at Teepy Tribe will be putting together a little sensory play area for the kids, so you can park them here while you go on your shopping sprees. For the creative folks, there are batik workshops to have a go at too, courtesy of Tumadi Batik.
 Admission: Free
 Venue: 1 Raffles Boulevard, Suntec Singapore Convention & Exhibition Centre, Hall 403, Singapore 039593
 Date: 7th-8th November 2026
 Time: Sat 4pm-10pm | Sun 11am-10pm
 9. Toy Story | PEACEMINUSONE: The First Fan pop-up 
 16th Oct till 11th Nov 
 View this post on Instagram 
 Head on over to the Toy Story | PEACEMINUSONE: The First Fan pop-up for a piece of G-Dragon’s unbridled, yet playful creativity. The King of K-pop’s fashion and lifestyle brand PEACEMINUSONE has joined hands with Disney’s Toy Story to bring fans of all ages a world of whimsy over at CQ @ Clarke Quay .
 You’ll be able to snap pics with Woody and gang , who’re all impeccably dressed in special get-ups that sport the Korean brand’s iconic sunflower motif. Of course, you can’t go home without a memento, so be sure to cart out merch such as keychains, plushies, figurines, hats, tees, and tote bags featuring beloved characters like Buzz, Jessie, Bullseye, and Rex.
 Get tickets to Toy Story | PEACEMINUSONE: The First Fan pop-up .
 Admission: $12/pax
 Venue: 3A River Valley Road, CQ @ Clarke Quay, #01-02
 Date: 16th October-11th November 2026
 Time: 1pm-11pm, Daily 
 10. Deepavali Open House 
 17th Oct-8th Nov 
 Image credit: Indian Heritage Centre  
 The Indian Heritage Centre is kickstarting the Deepavali festivities ahead of time with their annual Deepavali Open House . It’s free for all to pop by to experience the wonders of the festival of light, and it’s packed with plenty of family-friendly activities, perfect for filling out a weekend or 2.
 Image credit: Indian Heritage Centre  
 For maximum immersion, try on a community-loaned saree and strike a pose at the vintage photobooth on-site. Meanwhile, the creative minds can have a go at a couple of hands-on workshops, such as clay brooch painting and putting together your very own mini mithai box . A weekend bazaar will also be set up where you can bring home festive treats and accessories.
 Admission: Free
 Venue: 5 Campbell Lane, Indian Heritage Centre, Singapore 209924
 Date: Weekends from 17th October-8th November 2026
 Time: Sat 10am-8pm | 10am-6pm Sun
 11. Haw Ror Villa 5! – Back From The Dead 
 Now till 15th Nov 
 Should the crowd at USS’ Halloween Horror Night prove to be too frightening, Haw Par Villa’s annual scare fest is a good alternative. Dubbed Haw Ror Villa , it has returned to haunt Hell’s Museum for the 5th year running; make no mistake, it still packs a punch frights-wise, making it just the haunt for horror fans.
 It’s split into 4 zones, each themed differently and chock-full with suspense around every corner. Zone 1 serves as a precursor to the horrors ahead, as a court official from the 10 Courts of Hell sets the stage with an immersive performance . You’ll make your way through the Gateway of Hell in Zone 2, which is fraught with jumpscares, on top and puzzles to solve for an interactive experience.
 On that note, we’ll leave you to find out the rest of the perils that await. It takes around 2 to 2.5 hours to finish exploring all 4 zones, so we recommend having a decent meal before setting foot into this otherworldly attraction. FYI , you can pay for admission tickets to Haw Ror Villa 5! with your SG Culture Pass credits.
 Get tickets to Haw Ror Villa 5! – Back From The Dead .
 Admission: From $55/pax
 Venue: 262 Pasir Panjang Road, Haw Par Villa, Singapore 118628
 Date: Now till 15th November 2026
 Time: 6.30pm-12am, Daily 
 12. Sunflower Surprise: Garden by the Ocean 
 Now till 9th Nov 
 Image credit: Gardens by the Bay 
 This October, Gardens by the Bay is debuting its very first Portuguese-themed floral display Sunflower Surprise: Garden by the Ocean . No prizes for guessing which flower they’ll be spotlighting in this one; a sea of over 5,000 sunflowers across 20 varieties will engulf the Flower Dome, as the display faithfully recreates the country’s quaint coastal towns and picturesque countryside.
 Image credit: Gardens by the Bay 
 Expect to wander through a replica of Alfama , one of Lisbon’s oldest neighbourhoods, snap pics by the striped houses of the Costa Nova fishing village, complete with a 6m-tall Farol de Belém lighthouse . You’ll also get to catch a glimpse of Portugal’s agricultural traditions, by exploring vineyards, olive groves, and cork oaks.
 Admission: From $12/adult | $8/child & senior
 Venue: 18 Marina Gardens Drive, Gardens by the Bay, Flower Dome Singapore 018953
 Date: 9th October-9th November 2026
 Time: 9am-9pm
 13. Bollywood Farms 
 Now till 31st Dec 
 We’ll have to unfortunately wave goodbye to an iconic Primary School excursion destination pretty soon, as Bollywood Farms will be shuttering at the end of 2026 . As such, take this chance to reminisce about the good ol’ days by swinging for one last look at the idyllic attraction.
 We did just that, and found that there’s plenty to see, do, and eat. Explore the 10-acre farm by embarking on a self-guided trail, on which you’ll be able to see their vegetable gardens and fruit-bearing trees . Snap pics by the lotus pond , one of the largest of its kind in Singapore, and frolic amongst the butterflies at the butterfly garden .
 Conclude your visit with a pit stop at the farm’s Poison Ivy Bistro , which whips up hearty servings of local delights such as Nasi Lemak and Nasi Ulam. Of course, all veggies used for their dishes here are all harvested right from the nearby gardens.

 14. CATS The Musical 
 Now till 22nd Nov 
Image credit: CATS The Musical 
 The legendary CATS The Musical is back in town after a long 7 years to captivate the masses with a flurry of intricate feline costumes, cat-like acrobatics, and iconic songs. Watch as a group of cats known as the Jellicles gather for their annual Jellicle Ball, as they introduce themselves through an elaborate sequence of song and dance.
 The Tony Award-winning musical also features scores from the acclaimed Andrew Lloyd Webber, best known for his work on The Phantom of the Opera, so strap in for a night of show-stopping musical numbers and dazzling choreography.
 Get tickets to CATS The Musical .
 Admission: From $68
 Venue: 10 Bayfront Avenue, Sands Theatre, Marina Bay Sands, B1-69/70, Singapore 018971
 Date: Now till 22nd November 2026
 15. ONE Ocean: Every Action Ripples 
 Now till 3rd Jan 2027 
 Make waves this June at Science Centre Singapore with a lineup of immersive science experiences for the whole fam. The big highlight is ONE Ocean: Every Action Ripples , a new multi-sensory exhibition opening on 30th May that takes visitors on a deep-sea adventure through 10 interactive zones featuring 360° ocean projections, free-roaming VR, spatial soundscapes, and hands-on installations.
 Expect everything from Arctic expeditions and coral reefs to whale migrations and Singapore’s own marine ecosystems, all wrapped up in a visually stunning experience that feels part science museum, part underwater fever dream.
 There’ll also be ocean-themed activities under JUNEureka 2026, special KidsSTOP™ programmes, and school holiday activities happening throughout the month.
 Get tickets for ONE Ocean: Every Action Ripples .
 Admission: $18/adult | $13/child
 Venue: Science Centre Singapore, Annexe Halls
 Dates: From 30th May onwards
 Time: Tue-Sun 10am-5pm
 Find things to do in Singapore this weekend 
 We’re sure you have more than enough activities to fill your upcoming weekend. If not, check out our ultimate list of things to do in Singapore or the best attractions and activities in Singapore . If you’re looking for pretty places to snap lots of photos, hit up these Instagrammable places in Singapore while you’re at it.
 And those looking to plan their calendars in advance can check out our full list of upcoming live performances in 2026 .
